compensating.why: hop 1 always lowers the nesting level
hop 2 counts an Object as having at least one entry

ownership_reason: Only the gold decides what is written before the closing marker of a value: the indenter's indentation at the marker's level when the value has entries, a single space otherwise, then the marker itself. Hop 1 only computes the nesting level after the Object (and returns it for the facade's write-back of _nesting), hop 2 only binds the Object's marker '}', and hops 3 and 4 pass the generator, indenter, level, entry count and marker along unchanged; no hop writes anything after the gold returns. Once the gold has written '}' directly after '{', the space of the layout can appear only if a caller writes it itself or hands the gold fabricated inputs. The gold's javadoc promises the pretty-printed layout of DefaultPrettyPrinter, which closes a value without entries as '{ }' / '[ ]'; the variant writes '{}'. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the intact sibling DefaultPrettyPrinter.writeEndArray does the same step (`else { g.writeRaw(' '); }` for an array without values) and is used in production by WriterBasedJsonGenerator.writeEndArray and UTF8JsonGenerator.writeEndArray; testSystemLinefeed, testCustomSeparatorsWithPP and testRootSeparator pass through the chain (an Object with entries closed on the indentation of its level, the level dropping back after a nested Object, a NopIndenter Object closed with no white space).
